ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR per-share figures are per ordinary share while the Nasdaq price is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x10 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-24): cover page registers American Depositary Shares, each representing ten ordinary shares (NASDAQ: HTHT); ordinary shares listed on HKEX (1179)

capex_override.ack_reason: Out-of-band by construction: the band anchors on the last value filed under an engine-read tag, and H World has never filed capex under any such tag in companyfacts (last_filed_value is null; financials_history.csv shows capex blank/assumed-zero in every year), so every value flags out-of-band. This is not an unanchored estimate — it is the filer's own cash-flow statement figure for FY2025 (see source), and no engine-readable filed capex value exists in any period to anchor to.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads (the 20-F cash-flow line 'Purchases of property and equipment' is not carried in EDGAR companyfacts under PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment or any candidate). The engine applies this single FY2025 filing value to every missing period; against the true per-year figures in the same statement it understates FY2023 capex by RMB66M (RMB894M filed) and FY2024 by RMB55M (RMB883M filed) — slightly aggressive in direction but immaterial (~0.8% of those years' operating cash flow of RMB7,674M / RMB7,518M), and FY2025 is exact. Declared in RMB (the reporting currency); the engine FX-converts at period-end ECB rates.
capex_override.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-04-24), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Purchases of property and equipment': RMB828M for FY2025 (US$119M in the filing's own convenience-translation column), with RMB883M for FY2024 and RMB894M for FY2023 in the same statement

moat_against: Returns are not through-cycle proven: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json was 0.27% (FY2021) and -0.68% (FY2022) in the COVID trough before recovering to 10.37% / 21.72% / 11.94% (FY2023-25) — earnings power is hostage to the China travel cycle and RevPAR

H World International (ex-Deutsche Hospitality / Steigenberger) is a leased-hotel drag: HWI revenue -5.8% YoY in Q2 2026 as leased hotels are exited, and lease liabilities are large ($3,879M in dcf_numbers.json) against a thin equity base
Competition is dense and brands are replicable at the economy/midscale end: Jin Jiang, BTG Homeinns and Atour contest the same tier-1-4 cities; franchisees multi-home and own the real estate
Growth is shifting to lower-tier cities (pipeline 3,089 hotels at June 30, 2026) where fee density per room is lower, and group FY2026 revenue guidance is only 4%-8% including HWI
China/VIE/regulatory overhang: VIE structure, PRC regulation, US ADS tail risk, and founder/concentrated governance
moat_for: Scale network in China lodging: 13,539 hotels / 1,335,445 rooms in operation at June 30, 2026 (Q2 2026 results), with Hanting and JI Hotel the dominant economy/midscale brands — density rivals cannot quickly replicate
Asset-light manachise/franchise engine: 93% of rooms are M&F (Q2 2026), and M&F revenue grew +25.2% YoY in Q2 2026 to RMB3.6B — franchisees fund the capex, H World collects fees
Direct distribution: H Rewards membership and member bookings reduce OTA dependence and give pricing/revenue-management leverage (HWC ADR +2.6% YoY and RevPAR +1.1% YoY in Q2 2026)
Proven low-cost operating system for economy/midscale hotels (standardized design, central reservation and procurement) — a structural cost advantage in its segment
moat_justification: China's dominant economy/midscale hotel platform: 13,539 hotels and 1.34M rooms (Q2 2026), the Hanting/JI brand pair, a direct-membership distribution base and an asset-light model that is now 93% manachised/franchised rooms, with M&F revenue +25.2% YoY in Q2 2026. That is real scale, brand and cost advantage in its segment. Capped at 6 because the measured return history does not clear a wide-moat bar through a cycle: roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) was near zero/negative in FY2021-22 (0.27%, -0.68%) and recovered to 10.37% / 21.72% / 11.94% in FY2023-25 — good, not consistently well above the cost of capital, and the series is COVID-broken. Gross margin is not presented in the filing-direct data (fundamentals.json gross_profit/cogs are null — the 20-F presents hotel operating costs, not COGS), so no gross-margin claim is made. Against the moat: dense competition (Jin Jiang, BTG, Atour), franchisee multi-homing, the leased HWI drag in Europe, large lease liabilities, and China/VIE overhang. A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years.
name: H World Group Limited
one_liner: China's dominant economy/midscale hotel platform going asset-light, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $46.50: weighted IRR 12.94% (Tier C), weighted IV@15% $37.90 vs $46.50 price on the normalized median base OE of $2.82/ADS, with a bear-to-bull tier band of D to B — it clears 15% only at or below ~$37.90, and sized to the bear end (IV@15% $26.46).
